To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we can select topically important sentences from texts using a novel method based on topic models (b) we can select relevant gap phrases from each sentence by training a discriminative classifier using human annotated data (c) we can automatically choose distractors that have both contextual and semantic fit with the gap phrase by using a combination of a lexical similarity measure and a contextual similarity measure.

(1) we propose a sentence selection method that uses the topic distribution of a sentence to rank its importance; (2) we collected human annotations on the relative relevance scores of gap phrases and used this data to build a classifier to predict the relative relevance scores; and (3) we propose a method to select multiple-choice distractors based on their semantic similarity and contextual fit to the question.
